Freedom fighter Sakhina now battling old age and illness
2025-03-26T14:03:21+06:00 | Our Correspondent, Kishoreganj
https://www.thedailystar.net/news/bangladesh/news/freedom-fighter-sakhina-now-battling-old-age-and-illness-3858051

Freedom fighter Sakhina Begum, who killed six razakars with a scythe, is now bedridden and suffering from respiratory problems.

Born in Gurui village in Kishoreganj, she lost her husband, Kitab Ali, before the Liberation War .

Now 92, Sakhina joined the armed struggle, motivated by the death of her nephew, Matiur Rahman, who was martyred by the Pakistani army and razakars.

During the war, Sakhina worked as a cook for the freedom fighters and gathered intelligence on the collaborators' movements.

Her contributions were significant; she was captured by Pakistani forces but managed to escape and later used a scythe to kill at least five Razakars who had terrorised her community.

Her scythe is now preserved in the Liberation War Museum in Dhaka, serving as a testament to her bravery.

Birangona Women of Bangladesh

In recognition of her heroism, Sakhina received a grant of Tk 50,000 from the government in 1998 and currently receives a monthly freedom fighter's allowance.

Sakhina now lives in the Baramaipara area of Hilochia, where she is cared for by her niece, Fairunnesa Akhter.

Due to her age and health issues, she has lost much of her mobility and relies on Fairunnesa for assistance with daily tasks.

The Tk 20,000 allowance she receives is primarily used to buy her medicine. Despite her illness, Sakhina values visits from others, finding comfort in their presence.

"When someone comes to see me, it brings me joy," she said. "I feel less alone in my struggles."

Fairunnesa added, "It's difficult, but I want to do my best for her. She has given so much to our country, and now it's my turn to support her."

Chandali Mia, a local freedom fighter, said many like Sakhina played a vital role in the Liberation War, fighting alongside men to resist the occupation forces.

"Sakhina's bravery inspired many of us," he said.

Sakhina's legacy continues to inspire her community.

As she reflects on her life, Sakhina said, "I fought for my country, and I will always be proud of that. I hope the younger generation remembers our sacrifices."
